title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues Grothendieck's group-theoretic analysis of the profinite 'Teichmüller tower' in genus 0 and of the equation of loops. The reading below is inferred from the notation and the neighbouring pages.
- M is a profinite group of (outer-type) automorphisms of the fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,∞}.
- Π̂ ⊂ Ŝ^+ with Ŝ^+/Π̂ = S_3. Ŝ^+ is apparently the profinite orbifold fundamental group of the S_3-quotient (an extension of S_3 by Π̂). Π̂_0 is an index-type subgroup.
- μ = {±1}.
- ρ and σ appear to be torsion elements of order 3 and order 2: the S_3-stabilisers of the orbifold points.
- γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Γ̃_Q is a 'Galois-type' quotient, a GT-like group or Gal(Q̄/Q).
- N*_ρ is the normaliser-type subgroup attached to ρ, and Z_ρ the corresponding centraliser.

Previous pages. Grothendieck did the order-2 case (σ) there. N^{*!}_{σ,0} = N*_σ ∩ M^!_0 maps isomorphically onto γ_{ρ,σ}. Writing M(1/2) for it, he gets semidirect decompositions M^!_0 ≅ M(1/2)·Π̂_0, M^! ≅ M(1/2)·Π̂, M ≅ M(1/2)·Ŝ^+. In other words M(1/2) is a 'Galois section' attached to the S_3-fixed rational point 1/2.

This page: the order-3 analogue.
- Proposition. The map N^{*!}_{ρ,0} → γ_{ρ,σ} = Γ̃_Q is injective. Its image is the index-2 subgroup Γ'_{ρ,σ} = {γ | ε_3(γ) = 1}. Here ε_3 is the sign character (cyclotomic mod 3 / the S_3-sign) controlling whether γ fixes or swaps the two order-3 fixed points.
- Corollary. N^{*!}_{ρ,0} = Z^!_{0,ρ} := Z_ρ ∩ M^!_0.
- (142) He names this group M(-j). The capital J in the manuscript is presumably j = e^{2πi/3}, so -j = e^{-iπ/3}, a fixed point of z ↦ 1/(1-z). The point is defined only over Q(√-3) = Q(μ_3), which explains why the image is only the index-2 subgroup Γ'_Q.
- Second display (142). N^{*!}_ρ = N^{*!}_{ρ,0} × μ = Z^!_ρ = Z^!_{ρ,0} × μ.
- (143). M(-j) is a section of M' over γ'_{ρ,σ} ≅ Γ'_Q, where M' is the preimage of the index-2 subgroup. This gives semidirect decompositions:
  - M'^!_0 ≅ M(-j)·Π̂_0
  - M'^! ≅ M(-j)·Π̂
  - M'^♮ ≅ M(-j)·Ŝ
  - Z^!_ρ ≅ M(-j) × μ
  - Z^♮_ρ ≅ M(-j) × L_ρ
- A crossed-out final remark notes that μ_{z'} = {1, z'} normalises L_ρ, hence Z_ρ.

Next page. Grothendieck shows that the corresponding extension Γ̃_{ρ,σ} of Γ_{ρ,σ} by μ is non-trivial.

Modern reading. This is the profinite-group form of the Galois sections of π_1 of the orbifold [P^1 - {0,1,∞} / S_3] (≈ M_{1,1}-type) at its two orbifold points:
- j = 1728 / z = 1/2, rational, stabiliser of order 2;
- j = 0 / z = -ω, defined over Q(μ_3) on the cover, stabiliser of order 3.
In the combinatorial setting it amounts to normalisers of the torsion elements of order 2 and 3 in the (Galois/GT)-enlarged group.
errors: Page looks consistent. One structural point: the section M(-j) exists only over the index-2 subgroup Γ'_Q, not over all of Γ̃_Q. Grothendieck states this correctly. The asymmetry with the M(1/2) case is precisely the field-of-definition issue for -j.
No proofs are given on this page. The Proposition presumably follows from the analysis of ε_3 at the end of page 616 (ε_3 must equal 1), but the surjectivity onto Γ' is not argued here.
Some decorations (♮ vs *, !) are ambiguous in the handwriting. The identifications Z^!_ρ ≅ M(-j) × μ vs M^!(-j) × μ are slightly inconsistent in the manuscript itself.

ideas.what: Normaliser/centraliser of the order-3 torsion element maps isomorphically onto the index-2 subgroup of the Galois-type group cut out by the character ε_3.
ideas.modern_name: Galois section of the orbifold fundamental group at the orbifold point j=0 (fixed point -ω of the S_3 action), defined over Q(μ_3); normalisers of torsion in GT-type groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (GT and torsion of mapping class groups, 1997); Ihara–Matsumoto; also related to Grothendieck's own Longue Marche remarks on special points
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in La Longue Marche (1981) regarding privileged points 1/2 and -j; unsure

ideas.what: Semidirect decompositions M'^! ≅ M(-j)·Π̂, M' ≅ M(-j)·Ŝ, i.e. splitting of the automorphism group extension via the section at -j.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the outer Galois/GT representation via a (tangential or orbifold) base point section

ideas.what: Direct-product decompositions Z_ρ^! = M(-j) × μ: the sign group μ = {±1} splits off in the order-3 case. This contrasts with the non-trivial μ-extension Γ̃ studied on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting obstruction of Galois actions to Aut versus Aut/{±1}; non-split μ_2-central extensions

missed.claim: Explicit, systematic treatment of the two orbifold-point sections M(1/2) and M(-j) as subgroups of the automorphism group. The -j section lives only over the index-2 subgroup ker ε_3, with full decomposition tables for each layer (M^!_0, M^!, M, Z_ρ). This is a carefully worked unpublished detail, though the underlying facts are known in the Galois–Teichmüller literature.
missed.quote: Le sous-groupe Z^!_{0,ρ}=M(-J) est une section de M' sur γ'_{ρ,σ} ≃ Γ'_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant to section-conjecture-type questions for orbifold curves (M_{1,1}). Also relevant to GT versions incorporating order-2 and order-3 torsion (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps). Mainly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck worked this out explicitly.

deep.surprise_reason: A worked-out but essentially known structure: Galois sections at the orbifold points 1/2 and -j, with the field-of-definition index-2 phenomenon. It anticipates later work on GT and torsion elements, but nothing here seems absent from the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: 'N_ρ^α' should read N*_ρ (star), consistent with surrounding pages.
'Lemme [?]' at top: likely a crossed-out word before 'Proposition'.
'M(-J)': the J is presumably j (cube root of unity), i.e. the point -j.
'Comme N^{*!}_ρ ⊃ Z_ρ^! ∋ μ, on voit que l'on a'; the 'lim.' is probably 'l'on a'.
First line of (142) bis: N^{*!}_{ρ} (not N^{α}_{ρα}).
'Z^♮_ρ ≃ M^♮(-J)×L_ρ' and 'M'^♮ ≃ M(-J).Ŝ' (the symbol is Ŝ, not 𝔊).
